notes.claim: Adding or subtracting a constant k to a function shifts its graph up or down by k units.
Adding or subtracting a constant k to the x term shifts the graph left or right along the x-axis.
The horizontal shift direction is a common trap: the misconception is to shift right because the 3 in f(x + 3) is positive.

sources.title: Graph transformations - Identifying and sketching related functions - Higher Maths Revision - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Adding or subtracting a constant (k) to a function has the effect of shifting the graph up or down vertically by (k) units.

sources.title: Graph transformations - Identifying and sketching related functions - Higher Maths Revision - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Adding or subtracting a constant (k) to the (x) term has the effect of shifting the graph left or right along the (x)-axis.
